newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ASX to use Internet for local capital raising.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ASX to use Internet for local capital raising.

text.p: The Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) said on Thursday it expected to use the Internet to help small Australian companies raise capital.

"Before the end of the year, I expect that ASX will be using the Internet in an innovative way to help Australian companies, particularly the smaller ones, to raise capital," ASX managing director Richard Humphry said in a speech to a Chartered Institute of Company Secretaries in Australia (CICSA) seminar.
"Our plan is to provide a system that will bring investors and issuers together, but without any formal market structure," Humphry said.
Humphry said the facility would be part of the exchange's existing World Wide Web site, which is used to provide market information.
"It is our belief that such a system will be much more practical benefit than a so-called 'second board' or an alternative market, for trading small company shares," he said.

"You've heard people say that what Australia needs is a local NASDAQ, but the fact is that ASX's criteria for listing are already lower than NASDAQ's. The real problem that smaller companies have is in raising equity capital," he said.
Humphry said NASDAQ has developed a specialised information structure that makes it the centre for research, analysis and information about high-technology industry.

"In a similar way, we believe that we have a reasonable chance of making ASX the world centre for resource stocks," Humphry said. He said the ASX already has one of the major markets in resources, based largely on Australia and Paupa New Guinea, but also with stocks from Asia and North America.
"What we need to do now is to further develop our unique research and analysis capability for this sector in Australia, covering the world," he said.
